newsitem.title: FRANCE: Japanese N-waste nears Panama Canal -Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: Japanese N-waste nears Panama Canal -Greenpeace.

text.p: A shipment of nuclear waste from Japan is expected to enter the Panama Canal on Friday on its way to reprocessing plants in France and Britain, the environmental group Greenpeace said on Thursday.

The cargo of spent nuclear fuel, loaded in four containers aboard the British-flagged Pacific Pintail, came from Hokuriku Electric Power Co Inc's Shika nuclear power plant and left Japan three weeks ago, Greenepeace-France said in a statement.
The cargo should arrive in Europe in another two weeks, Greenpeace said. Half of the shipment is headed for France's La Hague reprocessing plant and the other half for Britain's Sellafield plant.

"Transporting nuclear fuel poses numerous safety and environmental problems," Greenpeace official Mike Tannsley said in a statement. "In shipping these dangerous materials to Europe for reprocessing, Japan is only transferring the environmental risk to other countries."

Greenpeace said the La Hague plant, operated by state-controlled nuclear firm Cogema, reprocessed nuclear fuel under contracts with Germany, Japan, Belgium, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Sweden and Spain.
It said British Nuclear Fuel Ltd's Sellafield plant reprocessed nuclear fuel under contracts with Japan, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Sweden and the Netherlands.
